nodes.definition: Treat the extraction system's outlet as a shop output with its own rules, distinct from the worker-protection reason the extraction exists. The gold line has real emission potential: the cyanide route can carry cyanide mist from agitation and gassing and the hot alkaline bath's own vapour, the sulfite route can release sulfur dioxide if anything acidic reaches it and ammonia from ammoniacal chemistry at temperature, and the pretreatment line contributes acid mist and hydrogen and oxygen from electrocleaning. The unit asks three questions: whether the outlet needs a permit or notification in this jurisdiction, which is a rule-register row rather than an assumption; what control is fitted between the tanks and the outside, typically lidded tanks, capture hoods and a scrubber or filter chosen against the supplier's specification; and what becomes of the control media, because saturated scrubber packing, filter media and scrubber liquor are contaminated with the very chemistry they captured and therefore become characterized waste streams rather than maintenance rubbish.

included: the outlet as a permit-or-notification question for the rule register
lidded tanks and capture as emission reduction as well as bath-life measures
scrubber or filter media and liquor as their own waste streams
maintenance cadence for control media as a compliance item
excluded: ventilation as worker exposure protection, PPE and monitoring, which are the chemical-safety sibling KB
stating emission limits or stack test requirements as fact
designing or specifying ventilation engineering, which is a qualified engineer's work

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an authority's position on the outlet, or a chemistry or extraction system change

pros.claim: Lidded tanks and good capture cut emissions, evaporation and drag-out heating losses at the same time
pros.example: lids on the hot gold bath reducing both vapour to the extraction and the make-up water the bath needs

pros.claim: Naming control media as a waste stream closes a gap that otherwise sends contaminated packing to the bin
pros.example: spent scrubber packing from a cyanide line entering the cyanide-bearing waste route rather than a skip

cons.claim: Scrubbing adds a maintenance stream and a running cost for a hazard the shop cannot see
cons.example: scrubber liquor needing periodic replacement and collection with nothing visibly wrong to justify it

cons.claim: Whether a small shop's outlet is regulated at all is genuinely unclear without asking, which invites doing nothing
cons.example: a bench shop assuming a domestic-scale extract fan cannot possibly be a permitted emission point

failure_modes: treating the extraction outlet as invisible because it points at the sky
disposing of saturated scrubber packing, filters or liquor as general maintenance waste
letting control media run past their service life so the control exists on paper only
assuming a scrubber sized for one chemistry handles a newly introduced one
acceptance_tests: the rule register carries a dated row for the extraction outlet naming the authority and the confirmation status
every control medium (packing, filter, liquor) appears on the waste inventory with a characterization and a route
a maintenance and replacement cadence for control media exists and is logged
revisit_triggers: a new chemistry with different emission potential enters the line
the extraction or scrubber system is modified or relocated
an authority confirms or changes the permitting position for the outlet
odour, fume or condensate complaints arise

nodes.definition: Own the waste side of an incident: once the immediate response is over, a spill has manufactured a brand-new waste stream that nobody characterized in advance. Contaminated absorbent, sweepings, gloves and clothing, the wash water used on the floor, anything in the secondary containment and any damaged container all become material with a class, and the class is inherited from the worst chemistry involved. Two rules dominate. First, a spill is never washed to a drain — the wash water is captured, and if the shop cannot capture it the spill is contained and absorbed rather than rinsed. Second, if two classes met during the incident, the residue is treated as the more hazardous class and, where cyanide and acid were both involved, the situation stops being a cleanup and becomes an emergency for trained responders under the chemical-safety readiness plan. The waste-side work is then to segregate the residue into its class container, characterize it as a distinct stream with the incident date, and feed the incident back into the segregation map so the layout that allowed it is changed.

included: spill residue, contaminated absorbent, clothing and wash water as a characterized stream
never-to-drain rule for spill wash water
worst-class inheritance when chemistries met
feeding the incident back into the segregation map
excluded: spill response readiness, kits, drills, signage and evacuation, which are the chemical-safety sibling KB
exposure first aid and medical response, which route to trained responders and professional care
insurance and liability handling

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an incident occurs, or a review shows residue routes or containment were inadequate

pros.claim: Naming the residue as a stream in advance means the cleanup does not end with an unlabeled bucket of unknown material
pros.example: a spare labeled container per chemistry class kept beside each bund specifically for cleanup residue

pros.claim: Feeding incidents back into the layout fixes causes rather than repeating cleanups
pros.example: moving the pickle drum out of the transfer path after a knocked-over container

cons.claim: Post-incident work competes with the urge to clean up and move on, so it is the step most often skipped
cons.example: residue left in an unmarked bag over a weekend because the shop wanted the floor clear before customers arrived

cons.claim: Worst-class inheritance can make a small spill produce disproportionately expensive waste
cons.example: a litre of spilled solution generating a full drum of absorbent that must be routed as cyanide-bearing

failure_modes: hosing a spill to a floor drain because it is 'mostly water'
bagging contaminated absorbent as general rubbish
combining residues from an incident that involved two classes into one container
closing out the incident without changing the layout or practice that caused it
acceptance_tests: labeled residue containers exist per chemistry class before any incident occurs
the written practice states that spill wash water is captured and never drained
each incident produces a dated characterization sheet for its residue and a recorded layout or practice change
revisit_triggers: any spill, leak or near-miss occurs
a container or bund fails
the shop layout or transfer routes change

nodes.definition: Assemble the file that lets the shop reconstruct, months later and under question, where every litre and every gram went. The set is specific: the rule register with its confirmation dates; a characterization sheet per stream with its evidence; container inspection and pickup logs; consignment or manifest copies with their signed returns; verified permit copies for each hauler, destination and reclaimer; reclaim shipment records and settlement statements; incident records with their residue characterizations; and a pointer to the training records that live in the chemical-safety file rather than duplicating them here. Retention periods are a jurisdiction class, so the register supplies the number and the shop's own rule is the longer of that and its insurer's requirement. The test of the file is not that it exists but that it answers a question: pick any drum that left last year and the file should show what it was, how it was characterized, who took it, under what document, where it went, and what came back.

included: the record set enumerated and kept in one place
retention period as a jurisdiction class plus the insurer's requirement
the reconstruct-any-load test as the file's acceptance criterion
pointers to records owned by sibling domains rather than duplicates
excluded: training and competency records themselves, which are the chemical-safety sibling KB's file
product quality and claim records, which are the marking and consumer-rules sibling KB
stating a retention period in years as universal fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a failed reconstruct test, an audit finding, or a confirmed retention requirement

pros.claim: One reconstructable file converts scattered paperwork into a defence that works under inspection
pros.example: answering an inspector's question about a specific drum in minutes from the file rather than from memory

pros.claim: The record set doubles as the shop's own management data for volumes, costs and reclaim performance
pros.example: pickup logs showing rinse water dominating collection cost and justifying a cascade rinse

cons.claim: Record keeping is real recurring labour with no visible daily payoff
cons.example: logging container inspections weekly for a year without a single finding

cons.claim: A file that is technically complete can still fail the reconstruct test if it is organised by document type rather than by load
cons.example: consignment copies filed chronologically with no link to the characterization sheet they describe

failure_modes: filing consignments but never chasing the signed return copies
keeping records in three places (email, a drawer, a phone) so no reconstruction is possible
discarding records at an assumed retention age that was never confirmed
duplicating the chemical-safety training file here and letting the two versions diverge
acceptance_tests: picking any load that left in the past year, the file yields its characterization, container history, document, destination and return copy
each hauler, destination and reclaimer has a dated permit verification in the file
the retention period in use is attributed to a named authority requirement or to the insurer, not assumed
revisit_triggers: a retention or record-format requirement is confirmed or changed
an inspection, insurance review or customer audit is announced
a reconstruct test fails for any sampled load

nodes.definition: Run the shop-level programme that decides where effort and money go on the waste side, using the honest arithmetic that most compliance cost scales with volume and most volume is created upstream. The levers in rough order of leverage for a bench: drag-out reduction, which cuts gold loss and waste volume at once; a still rinse per tank, which converts loss into recoverable inventory; counterflow rinsing, which cuts water volume for a fixed cleanliness; right-sized purchasing and tank volumes, since a smaller bath is a smaller eventual dump and less metal locked up; extending bath service life through the bath-chemistry specialist's controls rather than through this KB; and consolidating collections so licensed pickups are economic. Against those sit the fixed costs that do not shrink: permit and licence work, container and bund provision, record keeping, and the minimum charges of licensed collection and reclaim. The programme's honesty rule is that no lever may reduce cost by reducing compliance — a cheaper number that comes from discharging, commingling or holding material past its limits is not a saving, it is an unbooked liability.

included: ranking volume-reduction levers by leverage for a bench-scale shop
separating variable waste cost from fixed compliance cost
collection consolidation within container and hold-time limits
the rule that no saving may come from reduced compliance
excluded: bath life extension chemistry itself, which is bath-chemistry work
pricing, quoting or business-model advice, which belongs to the plating-business specialist
stating cost figures, charges or savings percentages as universal

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured volume, cost or reclaim data after a lever is applied

pros.claim: Ranking levers stops a shop spending on visible equipment when a free practice change dominates
pros.example: a drain-dwell and racking change delivering more than a filtration upgrade bought for the same purpose

pros.claim: Separating fixed from variable cost makes the compliance budget predictable rather than resented
pros.example: seeing that permit and record work is a flat annual cost while rinse water is the part that actually scales

cons.claim: The programme's payoff is slow and partly invisible, so it loses to whatever is urgent
cons.example: a cascade rinse project deferred for a year of busy weeks while collection costs keep rising

cons.claim: Cost framing is exactly where the temptation to trade compliance for savings enters
cons.example: a proposal to reduce collections by holding drums longer, which trades money for a hold-time breach

failure_modes: counting a saving that comes from discharging, commingling or over-holding material
optimising the cheapest stream while ignoring the one that dominates volume
buying equipment before measuring where the volume and losses actually are
letting cost pressure erode the segregation or container discipline that the savings depend on
acceptance_tests: each proposed lever names the stream it reduces and the measurement that will show whether it worked
every claimed saving is checked against the compliance rules it might be borrowing from
fixed compliance costs are listed separately from volume-driven costs in the shop's own view of the programme
revisit_triggers: production volume changes materially
collection or reclaim charges change
a measured reduction fails to appear after a lever is applied

nodes.definition: Put a short, binding check between a booked job and the moment the tanks are switched on, so the waste side can stop a run before it creates material it cannot lawfully hold. The check asks: does every stream this job will generate have a characterized destination; is there container capacity for the volume the job will produce, including the rinse water and any dump the job triggers; are any containers approaching their hold limit or their fill limit; is a collection or reclaim shipment booked in time; are the hauler, destination and reclaimer permits currently valid; and is any outstanding incident, failed inspection or missing return copy still open. If any answer is no, the job waits, is re-scoped, or the blocking item is fixed first. The gate is deliberately blunt because the alternative is discovering mid-run that there is nowhere for the rinse water to go, at which point every remaining option is a bad one. It is also the specialist's standing statement that safety and compliance beat throughput and deadline wherever they meet.

included: a pre-run checklist covering destinations, capacity, hold and fill limits, booked collections, permit validity and open items
the authority to hold or re-scope a job on a waste-side failure
escalation when a customer or deadline pressures the gate
excluded: quality, adhesion and thickness release criteria, which are the quality specialist's gate
final legal sign-off, which is a human decision outside the shop's technical staff
commercial negotiation with the customer about the delay

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a gate failure, a mid-run capacity incident, or a change in the shop's job mix

pros.claim: A pre-run gate converts waste capacity from a mid-run surprise into a scheduling input
pros.example: discovering before switch-on that the rinse-water drum will fill halfway through a large barrel run, and booking collection first

pros.claim: A written gate gives a bench operator a defensible reason to say no under deadline pressure
pros.example: pointing to the open item on the checklist rather than arguing with a customer about their delivery date

cons.claim: The gate delays revenue and is the single most unpopular control in a busy shop
cons.example: holding a paid rush job because the cyanide-bearing drum is near its hold limit and no collection is booked

cons.claim: A checklist run as a formality gives false assurance while missing the item it exists to catch
cons.example: ticking capacity from memory rather than looking at the containers, and running out mid-batch anyway

failure_modes: running the check after the job has started, when holding costs a scrapped batch
waiving the gate for a valued customer or an urgent deadline
checking capacity by impression instead of inspecting containers
treating an open incident or missing return copy as a paperwork detail rather than a blocking item
acceptance_tests: the gate is recorded as passed, with its date and the person who ran it, before each production run or batch series
every gate failure recorded shows the job held or re-scoped and the blocking item resolved before the run proceeded
capacity and hold-limit answers reference an actual container inspection, not a recollection
revisit_triggers: any run proceeded without a recorded gate
a mid-run waste capacity or destination problem occurs
job mix changes so the gate's questions no longer match the streams generated
a permit lapse or missing return copy is discovered after the fact

edges.why_related: you cannot draw a segregation architecture until you know every stream that must be kept apart
characterization operates stream by stream on the enumerated list; an unlisted stream is never characterized
the classification scheme, the coding and the point at which analysis is mandatory come from the naming authority, not from the shop
container material, closure, labeling and storage class all follow from what the stream has been determined to be
drag-out work targets the specific tanks whose carry-out the inventory shows dominating loss and volume
a still rinse captures whatever drag-out remains after the mechanical levers have been applied, so reduction comes first
the flowing rinse train is sized for the residue the still rinse did not capture
a retired bath is routed by what it has become in service, which the end-of-life characterization establishes
routing to reclaim or disposal is a decision made per characterized stream, including its metal content and hazard class
the solids handling rules exist because filters and sludge are among the richest gold-bearing streams to be routed
the cyanide class obligations are only enforceable if the physical separation from acids already exists
the heavy-metal and corrosive classes of the pretreatment line are assigned by characterization before any handling rule applies
you can only negotiate accepted forms and lot terms once you know which streams you intend to send
the settlement terms define what number exists to be booked and when it becomes real
the consignment document describes the waste as characterized, and permit matching is done against those classes
discharge authority exists only if a named authority has granted it, which the rule register identifies and dates
whether the extraction outlet is a permitted or notifiable emission point is a jurisdiction question before it is an engineering one
residue is routed into the same class containers and bunds the segregation map already defines
the consignment documents, permit verifications and signed returns are the backbone of the record set
the mass balance supplies the loss numbers that tell the programme which lever is worth pulling
the gate answers its questions from the record set — permit validity, open items, pickup history — rather than from memory
cyanide-bearing rinses constrain the rinse train absolutely: their own tanks, their own collection, and no shared line or drain with any acid rinse
whether rinse water may ever leave by drain, and under what limits, bounds how the rinse train may be designed and sized
nickel-line and acid-line material must stay out of every reclaim container, which constrains what may be routed as gold-bearing
spent scrubber packing, filter media and liquor inherit the captured chemistry and must enter the solids handling class rather than maintenance rubbish
cost and throughput pressure pushes to release a job the gate would hold for capacity, hold-time or permit reasons
edges.resolution_rule: the gate wins without exception: a job is held or re-scoped until the blocking waste item is resolved, and the cost of the hold is recorded as a compliance cost rather than avoided by waiving the check

edges.why_related: returning still-rinse concentrate conserves gold but returns dragged-in contamination, bringing the bath's retirement forward
edges.resolution_rule: return only into the single parent bath the still rinse serves, and stop returning the moment the bath-chemistry specialist's contamination indicators rise; bath integrity and deposit quality beat gold conservation, and the concentrate then routes to reclaim instead

edges.why_related: reclaim economics reward accumulating a large lot while the cyanide class rewards getting hazardous material off site promptly
edges.resolution_rule: hazard class and container hold limits win: cyanide-bearing gold material ships on the compliant schedule even when the lot is uneconomically small, and lot economics are improved by consolidating with the reclaimer rather than by holding longer

edges.why_related: the shop's estimate of what a lot contains and the refiner's settled assay will differ, and the gap invites optimistic booking
edges.resolution_rule: only the settled assay may be booked or quoted as value; the shop's estimate stays labeled as a planning figure, and a persistent gap triggers the contract's sampling and dispute path rather than a change in the books

edges.why_related: cutting water volume saves collection cost but under-rinsing carries drag-in into the next tank and onto the part
edges.resolution_rule: the rinse-cleanliness criterion set by the process side is a floor that water reduction may not cross; volume is reduced by counterflow, still rinses and rinse-on-demand, never by rinsing below the criterion, and a staining or adhesion fault reverses the last change

edges.why_related: the contamination load a rinse train must remove is set by how much solution came out of the tank, so drag-out volume drives rinse water volume
a bath dump produces tank sludge, spent cartridges and anode bags in one event, so retirement creates a solids spike
an incident manufactures a stream that was never on the inventory, forcing a fresh characterization dated to the incident
containers are labeled, dated and inspected before a collection is booked, because the document must describe what is actually presented
the retirement sequence sends the drained solution and solids into the reclaim route first and only then routes the residue as waste
the unaccounted remainder in the mass balance is the measurement that tells the shop whether its drag-out practice is actually working
a queried or rejected consignment, or a receiver's incoming analysis, corrects a characterization the shop believed was settled
repeated gate holds for capacity or hold-time reasons are the clearest signal of which stream the minimisation programme should attack next
both are non-gold regulated streams that share the characterize-contain-document-ship skeleton while differing sharply in hazard severity and in why segregation matters

conflict_axes.name: safety_and_compliance_versus_throughput
conflict_axes.description: Every waste control costs time and capacity in a shop that is paid for finished work, so the pressure to run now and deal with the waste later is constant and structural.
poles: release the job and manage the waste afterwards
hold the job until the waste route is provably ready
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compliance and safety win wherever they meet throughput; the pre-run gate is the enforcement point and its holds are recorded as compliance cost rather than waived

conflict_axes.name: gold_recovery_versus_bath_contamination
conflict_axes.description: Returning still-rinse concentrate is the single biggest gold saving available to a bench, and it is also the fastest way to import dragged-in metals into a working bath.
poles: return every drop of concentrate as make-up
route concentrate to reclaim and protect the bath
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: return only into the parent bath and only while contamination indicators are clean; the moment they rise, the concentrate becomes a reclaim stream

conflict_axes.name: water_volume_reduction_versus_rinse_quality
conflict_axes.description: Contaminated rinse water is the largest routine disposal volume, but the rinse exists to protect the deposit and the next tank, and under-rinsing shows up as staining, poor adhesion and re-runs.
poles: rinse until the stated cleanliness criterion is met
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the process side's cleanliness criterion as a hard floor and get volume reduction from counterflow, still rinses and rinse-on-demand instead

conflict_axes.name: economic_lot_accumulation_versus_hold_limits
conflict_axes.description: Reclaimers and licensed haulers price for volume, so a bench shop is always tempted to hold hazardous or valuable material longer than its containers and its jurisdiction allow.
poles: accumulate until the lot or load is economic
ship on the compliant schedule regardless of lot size
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold limits and container condition govern; improve lot economics by consolidating streams and negotiating terms, never by extending time on site

conflict_axes.name: on_site_treatment_versus_ship_out
conflict_axes.description: Treating a stream on site looks cheaper than paying for licensed collection, and the classic cyanide destruction route is documented well enough to tempt a capable shop into trying it.
poles: neutralise, destroy or treat in house
ship out to a licensed destination under paperwork
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: ship-out is the bench-scale answer; treatment is a licensed, engineered and monitored operation whose feasibility is a question for the authority and a qualified engineer, never a bench experiment

conflict_axes.name: cheapest_handler_versus_verified_licensed_chain
conflict_axes.description: There is always someone who will take the drums for less, and the difference in price usually is the licence, the paperwork and the destination.
poles: use only verified licensed transporter and destination
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: verified permits covering the specific waste classes are a precondition for any quote to be considered; duty of care does not transfer with the drum

conflict_axes.name: estimated_metal_value_versus_settled_assay
conflict_axes.description: The shop can estimate what a drum holds long before the refiner settles it, and every commercial pressure favours treating the estimate as money.
poles: book only what the settlement statement says
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: settlement governs the books and any statement to a third party; estimates stay labeled as planning figures and a persistent gap goes to the contract's dispute path

conflict_axes.name: segregation_discipline_versus_bench_convenience
conflict_axes.description: One drum, one funnel and one bucket are faster and take less floor space than four of each, and convenience quietly erodes segregation exactly when the shop is busiest.
poles: keep a physically separate set per chemistry class
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: segregation is non-negotiable where cyanide and acid are involved and near-absolute elsewhere; convenience is bought by better layout, never by shared vessels

conflict_axes.name: capital_spend_versus_recurring_loss
conflict_axes.description: Still rinses, cascade tanks, bunds and scrubber maintenance need money now to reduce losses and collection volumes that are spread thinly across the year.
poles: defer capital and absorb recurring cost
invest in recovery and containment kit now
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: rank by measured leverage — drag-out and still rinse first because they are nearly free and pay in metal — and never fund capital by relaxing a control

edge_cases.description: Two chemistries end up in one drum during a busy week and the resulting liquid cannot be characterized from input knowledge at all
edge_cases.trigger: an unlabeled general-purpose container is used for more than one stream
edge_cases.mitigation: stop using the container immediately, isolate it in secondary containment away from all other classes, treat it as the most hazardous class that could plausibly be present pending accredited analysis, and close the layout gap that allowed a shared vessel to exist

edge_cases.description: A customer rework job requires stripping old plating, producing a stripping solution loaded with dissolved metal and an aggressive chemistry that is on nobody's stream list
edge_cases.trigger: a rework or refinishing job introduces a stream the inventory never anticipated
edge_cases.mitigation: add the stream to the inventory before the job is accepted, characterize it from the stripper's data sheet and the known substrate, give it its own container, and hold the job at the release gate until a destination exists

edge_cases.description: The reclaimer's settlement comes back far below the shop's estimate of the lot
edge_cases.trigger: assayed content and estimated content diverge materially
edge_cases.mitigation: do not adjust the books towards the estimate; use the agreement's sampling and dispute path, check whether the lot was diluted or commingled before shipping, and feed the gap back into the mass balance as a routing or drag-out finding

edge_cases.description: A booked collection is cancelled or delayed and containers approach both their fill limit and their accumulation hold limit
edge_cases.trigger: hauler delay, vehicle failure or a missed booking window
edge_cases.mitigation: hold production that generates the affected stream, document the delay and the reason, escalate to the hauler and to the authority if the hold limit will actually be crossed, and never solve it by decanting into unsuitable vessels or by discharging

edge_cases.description: A heater or power failure crashes a sulfite gold bath and metallic gold precipitates onto tank walls, the heater and the tank bottom
edge_cases.trigger: a bath instability event turns dissolved gold into a solid residue
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the precipitate as high-value gold-bearing solids collected separately from the solution, re-characterize both fractions at retirement, and never attempt to redissolve or acid-treat the residue on the bench

edge_cases.description: A spill is hosed towards a floor drain because the shop is trying to clear the area quickly
edge_cases.trigger: an incident happens during production and the reflex is to wash it away
edge_cases.mitigation: written practice is contain and absorb, never rinse; wash water is captured as residue; if it reached a drain, record it as a reportable incident, tell the authority per the rule register, and seal or bund the drain before work resumes

edge_cases.description: The shop is too small for any hauler to quote sensibly, and a five-litre stream sits with no economic route
edge_cases.trigger: volumes fall below a licensed collector's minimum load
edge_cases.mitigation: ask the authority about lawful options for very small generators, consolidate compatible streams within their class, share a collection with another compliant local shop only if the paperwork allows it, and treat 'no route yet' as a reason to pause that process rather than to improvise disposal

edge_cases.description: A legacy container with a faded label is found during a shop move or a change of ownership
edge_cases.trigger: unlabeled or unidentifiable material is discovered on site
edge_cases.mitigation: do not open, decant, smell or test it at the bench; isolate it away from every other class, arrange accredited sampling or a specialist collection for unknowns, and record the find and its resolution in the file

edge_cases.description: Scrubber packing or an extraction filter has been in service far past its replacement interval and is saturated with captured chemistry
edge_cases.trigger: control media maintenance is missed or the media is treated as a maintenance consumable
edge_cases.mitigation: replace on a logged cadence, route the spent media into the waste class of the chemistry it captured, and check whether the outlet's permitting position in the rule register was ever confirmed

edge_cases.description: A trade account asks the shop to take their spent plating solution as a favour or as part of a deal
edge_cases.trigger: another business offers or sends its waste to the shop
edge_cases.mitigation: decline unless the jurisdiction's rules for receiving another party's waste have been confirmed and the shop holds whatever standing that requires; accepting someone else's waste changes the shop's regulatory role and can invalidate its own arrangements

edge_cases.description: A rinse tank overflows during an unattended run and the water reaches a floor drain whose destination has never been confirmed
edge_cases.trigger: level control, a stuck valve or an overnight run fails
edge_cases.mitigation: stop the line, establish where the drain actually goes and record it, report per the rule register if a discharge occurred, seal or bund the drain, and add overflow containment before the tank is used again

workflow.action: Build the regulator and rule register
workflow.description: Name the authority for each output class, record the believed obligation, the evidence and the confirmation status
workflow.artifact: dated rule register with confirmed and unconfirmed rows
workflow.gate: every output class names an authority and carries either a dated confirmation or an explicit unconfirmed flag

workflow.action: Enumerate every stream that leaves the shop
workflow.description: Walk the whole wet line including pretreatment, consumables, solids and occasional streams
workflow.artifact: stream register with parent chemistry, form, gold-bearing flag and arrival rate
workflow.gate: every tank and consumable traces to at least one listed stream and each row is complete

workflow.action: Draw the segregation and drain map
workflow.description: Assign containers, storage areas, transfer equipment and spill kits per chemistry class and identify every drain
workflow.artifact: shop layout drawing with class zones and a drain destination map
workflow.gate: cyanide-bearing and acid-bearing waste are physically separate in container, bund, equipment and kit, and no drain of unknown destination remains in use

workflow.description: Determine hazard properties and class from data sheets and process log, or send for accredited analysis
workflow.artifact: characterization sheet per stream with evidence and date
workflow.gate: no stream lacks a sheet, and any stream with incomplete input knowledge is flagged for analysis and not moved

workflow.description: Select compatible containers, mark contents, hazard, process and start date, place in secondary containment and start the inspection log
workflow.artifact: labeled container set with bunds and a dated inspection log
workflow.gate: every container is compatible, closed, marked, contained and appears in the inspection log

workflow.description: Fix withdrawal rate, over-tank dwell and racking orientation per tank and per repeat part family
workflow.artifact: written drain-and-rack practice posted at the line
workflow.gate: the practice exists per tank and a drag-out proxy such as still-rinse fill rate is being tracked

workflow.action: Fit a still drag-out rinse per process tank
workflow.description: Dedicate one still rinse to each bath, define the return-as-make-up rule and the switch to reclaim routing
workflow.artifact: still rinse per tank, labeled to its parent bath, with a written return rule
workflow.gate: no still rinse serves two baths and the stop-returning condition is written down

workflow.description: Set counterflow cascades, changeover criteria and per-class rinse line separation, assuming containerised water
workflow.artifact: rinse train layout with per-class collection routes and changeover criteria
workflow.gate: each rinse tank belongs to one class, has a stated changeover criterion and a collection route that assumes no discharge permission

workflow.action: Route the gold-bearing streams to reclaim
workflow.description: Flag every gold-bearing stream including solids and consumables and give each a container and a destination
workflow.artifact: reclaim routing plan with dedicated labeled containers
workflow.gate: every stream is marked gold-bearing or not with a reason, and no reclaim container may receive nickel or acid material

workflow.action: Appoint and verify the reclaimer and the licensed handler
workflow.description: Verify transporter, destination and reclaimer permits against the actual waste classes and agree the reclaim terms
workflow.artifact: verified permit copies, the reclaim agreement and the consignment document template
workflow.gate: each class the shop moves has dated permit verification for both transporter and destination before any load leaves

workflow.action: Open and populate the records trail
workflow.description: Bring register, characterizations, inspections, consignments, returns, permits and settlements into one reconstructable file
workflow.gate: picking any load at random, the file reconstructs what it was, who took it, under what document and what came back

workflow.action: Run the pre-run waste release gate on every job
workflow.description: Check destinations, capacity, hold and fill limits, booked collections, permit validity and open items before switch-on
workflow.artifact: signed and dated gate record per run or batch series
workflow.gate: the gate is recorded before the run, and any failure shows the job held or re-scoped until the blocking item was resolved

priority_rationale: The frame units come first because nothing downstream is decidable without them: you cannot segregate streams you have not listed, cannot characterize against rules whose authority you have not identified, and cannot contain or ship what you have not characterized. Segregation and characterization then gate every stream-specific unit — cyanide, nickel and acid, solids, retired baths, spill residues — because each is only a rule applied to a class already established. The recovery units sit alongside them because drag-out, still rinses and rinse design change the size and value of every stream before it becomes waste. The off-site units (licensed transfer, discharge and emission permissions, records) come last among the doing units because they consume the characterizations and containers the earlier work produced, and the release gate is last of all because it is the composed check that every one of those layers is actually ready before a job is allowed to create more material.

dominance_rules.rule: Cyanide and acid segregation dominates every other consideration, including space, cost, convenience and schedule
dominance_rules.rationale: contact between the two liberates hydrogen cyanide, which is a fatal outcome rather than a compliance failure, and the same physical discipline also prevents sulfur dioxide release on the cyanide-free route
dominance_rules.trigger: any decision about containers, storage position, transfer equipment, drains or cleanup involving either class
dominance_rules.action: keep them physically separate in vessel, bund, equipment, kit and drain path; if separation cannot be maintained, stop the activity rather than compromise it

dominance_rules.rule: No-discharge dominates volume and cost pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: discharge authority is a written permission from a named authority; absent it, every litre is a container-and-manifest stream and dilution is never a treatment
dominance_rules.trigger: any proposal to put plating-line water, rinse water, floor wash or spill water into any drain
dominance_rules.action: refuse the discharge, keep the stream containerised, and route the question to the water authority as a permit application rather than a bench decision

dominance_rules.rationale: an uncharacterized container cannot lawfully be handed to anyone and cannot be described accurately on a consignment document
dominance_rules.trigger: any stream about to be moved, consolidated, shipped or handed over
dominance_rules.action: complete or update the characterization sheet first; if input knowledge is insufficient, arrange analysis and hold the material

dominance_rules.rule: A verified licensed chain dominates price
dominance_rules.rationale: the generator's duty of care does not transfer with the drum, so an unlicensed cheap collection remains the shop's liability
dominance_rules.trigger: selecting or renewing a hauler, destination or reclaimer, or accepting an unsolicited offer to remove waste
dominance_rules.action: verify current permits covering the specific classes before any quote is considered, and record the verification with its date

dominance_rules.rule: Hazard class and hold limits dominate reclaim economics
dominance_rules.rationale: the value of a larger lot never justifies keeping acutely hazardous material on site beyond its container and jurisdiction limits
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposal to accumulate longer to reach an economic lot or load
dominance_rules.action: ship on the compliant schedule and improve lot economics through consolidation and contract terms instead

dominance_rules.rule: Settled assay dominates estimated metal value in every record and every statement
dominance_rules.rationale: an estimate presented as realised value misleads customers, insurers, buyers and the shop itself
dominance_rules.trigger: any booking, quotation, valuation or claim involving recovered gold
dominance_rules.action: book and quote only settlement figures; keep estimates explicitly labeled as planning figures

dominance_rules.rule: The waste release gate dominates the delivery deadline
dominance_rules.rationale: waste created with nowhere lawful to go leaves only bad options, and the pressure to improvise is highest exactly when the deadline is closest
dominance_rules.trigger: a job is ready to run while any gate item is open
dominance_rules.action: hold or re-scope the job, resolve the blocking item, and record the hold as a compliance cost rather than waiving the check

dominance_rules.rationale: destruction and treatment of plating wastes are engineered, permitted and monitored operations, and the documented routes exist to explain why licensed destinations are used, not to be reproduced at a bench
dominance_rules.trigger: any suggestion to neutralise, destroy, precipitate, evaporate or otherwise treat a stream on site
dominance_rules.action: route the material to the licensed destination and refer any genuine treatment ambition to the authority and a qualified engineer before any chemistry is attempted

dominance_rules.rule: The jurisdiction's own rule dominates every generic source, including this knowledge base
dominance_rules.rationale: codes, thresholds, hold times, document names and retention periods are local and change, while only the classes and mechanisms are general
dominance_rules.trigger: any question of a number, a code, a hold time or a legal duty
dominance_rules.action: take the answer from the naming authority or a qualified adviser, record it in the register with its date, and treat any unconfirmed row as unresolved rather than permissive

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the rule register before buying containers, plumbing tanks or booking a hauler
anti_rework_rules.prevents: committing to storage, drainage and collection arrangements that the actual authority does not accept, then rebuilding them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Characterize before you pour, consolidate or move anything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an uncharacterizable mixed container that no receiver will accept and that costs analysis money to resolve

anti_rework_rules.rule: Segregate at the tank rather than trying to separate at the drum
anti_rework_rules.prevents: having to treat every mixed stream as the worst class present, multiplying both hazard handling and disposal cost

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fit the still drag-out rinse before scaling production volume
anti_rework_rules.prevents: gold and rinse-water volume losses that cannot be recovered retrospectively once the material has left

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label and date every container at its first drop, not when collection is booked
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unidentifiable legacy containers that require sampling, specialist collection and an incident record

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree the reclaimer's weighing, sampling, assay and settlement terms before shipping the first lot
anti_rework_rules.prevents: settlement disputes with no procedure to invoke and lots already refined beyond re-examination

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify hauler and destination permits before the first collection, not after an inspection asks
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unlawful transfer that cannot be undone and that taints every load already moved on the same arrangement

anti_rework_rules.rule: Book collection capacity against the planned production schedule before accepting the work
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a mid-run stop with full containers, an unfinished batch and a customer promise that cannot be kept lawfully

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record the process history alongside each container as it fills
anti_rework_rules.prevents: paying for laboratory analysis to rediscover what the shop already knew when the drum was being filled

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reclaim settlement lands materially below the shop's estimate
iteration_protocol.action: re-examine routing, check for commingling or dilution before shipping, invoke the contract's sampling path, and re-run the period mass balance

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new chemistry, additive, supplier or process step is introduced
iteration_protocol.action: add its streams to the inventory, re-characterize, re-check the segregation map and update the rule register rows it touches

iteration_protocol.trigger: an annual review date, a permit renewal or a regulator contact
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify every register row and every handler permit, and re-date the confirmations

iteration_protocol.trigger: containers approach fill or hold limits, or a collection is delayed
iteration_protocol.action: hold the production that feeds the affected stream, escalate the collection, and record the delay and its resolution

iteration_protocol.trigger: a receiver queries, rejects or re-analyses a consignment
iteration_protocol.action: correct the characterization sheet, re-describe the affected stream, and check whether other streams share the same wrong assumption

iteration_protocol.trigger: a spill, leak, overflow or near-miss occurs
iteration_protocol.action: characterize the residue as a dated stream, re-walk the segregation and containment layout, and change the arrangement that allowed it

iteration_protocol.trigger: staining, adhesion or spotting faults appear after a water or drag-out change
iteration_protocol.action: reverse the most recent rinse or dwell change, restore the cleanliness criterion, and find the volume saving somewhere that does not touch rinse quality

iteration_protocol.trigger: production volume or job mix changes materially
iteration_protocol.action: recompute stream arrival rates, container capacity and collection cadence, and re-rank the minimisation levers against the new volumes
